decisions.reason: As an adjacent HVAC line in a growing, R&D-active firm with broad portfolio slack, its early performance is not clearly below aspiration, so management is likely to continue learning rather than withdraw it.
Reported major market share and fit with the established marine cooling business put results above aspiration, giving little reason for problemistic search or withdrawal.
This marine cooling unit is close to core capabilities and customer needs, and with no negative signal plus available organisational slack, management would likely keep it on the market.
The compact oil cooler extends the existing offer and, in a favorable industry context with hiring and in-house R&D, is likely to be retained while its market acceptance becomes clearer.
A dedicated market presentation and strong related engineering capabilities suggest enough promise to stay above a minimal aspiration threshold, so the firm is likely to keep it.

Enhanced heat exchanger tubes build directly on the firm's technical base and service learning, and absent evidence of underperformance, boundedly rational management would usually continue rather than drop them.
